course.description: How finance professionals build dashboards, close trackers, and data tools with AI — no coding experience required.
learningOutcomes: Apply the methods taught in Building Apps with AI — From Idea to Deployed Tool.

lessons.content:
## Dashboards, Close Trackers, Data Tools

AI generates working code from plain English. If you can describe it, you can build it.

### Real Examples Finance Teams Are Building Today

- **Expense dashboards** — pull data from a Google Sheet, visualize spend by category, department, or period
- **Month-end close trackers** — status board showing which tasks are done, who owns what, what's overdue
- **Reconciliation templates** — upload two data sources, auto-match, surface exceptions
- **Compliance training games** — RPG-style SOX or policy training (yes, really)
- **Cash flow calculators** — input assumptions, get a 13-week cash forecast
- **Allocation engines** — define rules, run allocations, generate the JEs

### Why Google Apps Script?

Apps Script gives you a deployment platform **already inside your company's security perimeter:**
- Runs on Google's infrastructure — no server to manage
- Accessible to anyone with a Google account
- Integrates natively with Sheets, Docs, Gmail, Calendar
- Can be deployed as a web app with a URL your team can bookmark

> **Key insight:** You're not learning to code. You're learning to describe what you need clearly enough that AI can code it for you.
lessons.title: What Can You Build?

lessons.content:
## You Don't Need to Know How to Code

There are multiple ways to build with AI. Pick the one that matches your comfort level:

### 1. Claude.ai (Web) — Quick Prototypes
- Best for: one-off tools, calculators, visual artifacts
- How: describe what you want → Claude generates a working prototype → iterate
- Output: HTML/CSS/JS that runs in the browser

### 2. Claude Code (Terminal) — Real Applications
- Best for: production tools, multi-file projects, agent-powered apps
- How: describe the app in natural language → Claude writes the code → deploy
- Output: full applications with backend logic

### 3. OpenAI Codex — Autonomous Coding
- Best for: larger builds where you want AI to work independently
- How: give it a task → it codes, tests, and delivers
- Output: complete codebases

### 4. Google Apps Script — Google Sheets Tools
- Best for: anything that lives in or near a Google Sheet
- How: paste AI-generated code into the Script Editor → deploy as web app
- Output: web apps accessible via URL, sidebar tools in Sheets

### The Pattern Is Always the Same

```
You describe → AI builds first pass → You refine → Repeat
```

You don't need to understand the code. You need to understand your workflow well enough to describe it.

> **The 5-Skill Loop:** Describe → AI first pass → You refine → Level up into a reusable agent, tool, or template

activities.title: Build AND Maintain — One Agent, One Tool, Forever

lessons.content:
## AI Doesn't Just Build Tools — It Owns Them

This is the insight most people miss:

### The Old Way
1. You build a tool (or IT builds it for you)
2. It works for a while
3. Something breaks or requirements change
4. You file a ticket, wait weeks, or abandon the tool

### The New Way
1. AI builds the tool
2. You assign an **engineer agent** to that tool
3. The agent that built it **maintains it, updates it, and fixes bugs**
4. One agent, one tool, forever

### What This Looks Like in Practice

You tell your agent:
> "The expense dashboard is showing last month's data. Update it to pull the current month."

The agent reads the code, understands the data source, makes the fix, and redeploys. No ticket. No waiting.

### From "I Built a Thing" to "I Have a Team of Agents"

| Stage | What You Have |
|-------|--------------|
| **Week 1** | One dashboard built by AI |
| **Month 1** | 3-4 tools, each with a maintenance agent |
| **Quarter 1** | A portfolio of tools + agents that self-maintain |
| **Year 1** | An agent organization running your function's tooling |

> **The endgame:** You're not a developer. You're a **manager of AI developers.**
lessons.title: Build AND Maintain — One Agent, One Tool, Forever

lessons.content:
## Go Do It — Right Now

### Option A: Claude Artifact (60 seconds)
1. Open [claude.ai](https://claude.ai)
2. Type: *"Build me a month-end close checklist tracker with status toggles, owner assignments, and a progress bar"*
3. You have a working tool in under a minute

### Option B: Apps Script Dashboard (5 minutes)
1. Create a new Google Sheet
2. Add your data (expenses, revenue, whatever you're tracking)
3. Open Claude and type: *"Write a Google Apps Script web app that reads data from my Google Sheet and displays it as a dashboard with charts"*
4. Paste the code into Extensions → Apps Script
5. Deploy → New Deployment → Web App
6. You have a live URL your team can access

### Option C: Full App with Claude Code (15 minutes)
1. Open your terminal
2. Type: `claude` to start Claude Code
3. Describe what you want: *"Build a reconciliation tool that takes two CSV uploads, auto-matches transactions by amount and date, and surfaces unmatched items"*
4. Claude builds it, you review, deploy

---

### Then Ask: What Else Does My Team Need?

Every tool you build saves time. Every tool that saves time is a business case. Every business case builds momentum for broader AI adoption.

- [Ore Phillips Guides](https://finney.finance/project/ore-phillips-guides)
